    20→// Note that forkchoice is used here in a lock-free fashion, assuming that a version of forkchoice
    21→// is given that internally handles the details of locking the underlying store.
    22→type Forkchoicer interface {
    23→	FinalizedCheckpoint() *forkchoicetypes.Checkpoint
    24→	HasNode([32]byte) bool
    25→	IsCanonical(root [32]byte) bool

    33→}

    35→// sharedResources provides access to resources that are required by different verification types.

    37→type sharedResources struct {

    40→	sc    signatureCache
    41→	pc    proposerCache
    42→	sr    StateByRooter

    51→}

    53→// NewBlobVerifier creates a BlobVerifier for a single blob, with the given set of requirements.

    55→	return &ROBlobVerifier{
    56→		sharedResources:      ini.shared,
    57→		blob:                 b,

    60→	}

    65→func (ini *Initializer) NewDataColumnsVerifier(roDataColumns []blocks.RODataColumn, reqs []Requirement) *RODataColumnsVerifier {
    66→	return &RODataColumnsVerifier{
    67→		sharedResources:             ini.shared,
    68→		dataColumns:                 roDataColumns,
    69→		results:                     newResults(reqs...),
    70→		verifyDataColumnsCommitment: peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs,
    71→		stateByRoot:                 make(map[[fieldparams.RootLength]byte]state.BeaconState),
    72→	}
    73→}

    75→// InitializerWaiter provides an Initializer once all dependent resources are ready
    76→// via the WaitForInitializer method.
    77→type InitializerWaiter struct {
    78→	sync.RWMutex
    79→	ready   bool
    80→	cw      startup.ClockWaiter
    81→	ini     *Initializer
    82→	getFork forkLookup
    83→}

    87→type InitializerOption func(waiter *InitializerWaiter)
    88→
    89→// WithForkLookup allows tests to modify how Fork consensus type lookup works. Needed for spectests with weird Forks.
    90→func WithForkLookup(fl forkLookup) InitializerOption {
    91→	return func(iw *InitializerWaiter) {
    92→		iw.getFork = fl
    93→	}
    94→}
    95→
    96→// NewInitializerWaiter creates an InitializerWaiter which can be used to obtain an Initializer once async dependencies are ready.
    97→func NewInitializerWaiter(cw startup.ClockWaiter, fc Forkchoicer, sr StateByRooter, opts ...InitializerOption) *InitializerWaiter {
    98→	pc := newPropCache()
    99→	// signature cache is initialized in WaitForInitializer, since we need the genesis validators root, which can be obtained from startup.Clock.
   100→	shared := &sharedResources{
   101→		fc: fc,
   102→		pc: pc,
   103→		sr: sr,
   104→		ic: newInclusionProofCache(defaultInclusionProofCacheSize),
   105→	}
   106→	iw := &InitializerWaiter{cw: cw, ini: &Initializer{shared: shared}}
   107→	for _, o := range opts {
   108→		o(iw)
   109→	}
   110→	if iw.getFork == nil {
   111→		iw.getFork = params.Fork
   112→	}
   113→	return iw
   114→}
   115→
   116→// WaitForInitializer ensures that asynchronous initialization of the shared resources the initializer
   117→// depends on has completed before the underlying Initializer is accessible by client code.
   118→func (w *InitializerWaiter) WaitForInitializer(ctx context.Context) (*Initializer, error) {
   119→	if err := w.waitForReady(ctx); err != nil {
   120→		return nil, err
   121→	}
   122→	// We wait until this point to initialize the signature cache because here we have access to the genesis validator root.
   123→	vr := w.ini.shared.clock.GenesisValidatorsRoot()
   124→	sc := newSigCache(vr[:], defaultSignatureCacheSize, w.getFork)
   125→	w.ini.shared.sc = sc
   126→	w.ini.shared.ic = newInclusionProofCache(defaultInclusionProofCacheSize)
   127→	return w.ini, nil
   128→}
   129→
   130→func (w *InitializerWaiter) waitForReady(ctx context.Context) error {
   131→	w.Lock()
   132→	defer w.Unlock()
   133→	if w.ready {
   134→		return nil
   135→	}
   136→
   137→	clock, err := w.cw.WaitForClock(ctx)
   138→	if err != nil {
   139→		return err
   140→	}
   141→	w.ini.shared.clock = clock
   142→	w.ready = true
   143→	return nil
   144→}

     2→
     3→import (
     4→	"github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/v6/beacon-chain/blockchain/kzg"
     5→	fieldparams "github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/v6/config/fieldparams"

    11→)
    12→
    13→const kzgPosition = 11 // The index of the KZG commitment list in the Body
    14→
    15→var (
    16→	ErrIndexTooLarge               = errors.New("column index is larger than the specified columns count")
    17→	ErrNoKzgCommitments            = errors.New("no KZG commitments found")
    18→	ErrMismatchLength              = errors.New("mismatch in the length of the column, commitments or proofs")
    19→	ErrInvalidKZGProof             = errors.New("invalid KZG proof")
    20→	ErrBadRootLength               = errors.New("bad root length")
    21→	ErrInvalidInclusionProof       = errors.New("invalid inclusion proof")
    22→	ErrRecordNil                   = errors.New("record is nil")
    23→	ErrNilBlockHeader              = errors.New("nil beacon block header")
    24→	ErrCannotLoadCustodyGroupCount = errors.New("cannot load the custody group count from peer")
    25→)
    26→
    27→// https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/fulu/p2p-interface.md#custody-group-count
    28→type Cgc uint64
    29→
    30→func (Cgc) ENRKey() string { return params.BeaconNetworkConfig().CustodyGroupCountKey }
    31→
    32→// VerifyDataColumnSidecar verifies if the data column sidecar is valid.
    33→// https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/fulu/p2p-interface.md#verify_data_column_sidecar
    34→func VerifyDataColumnSidecar(sidecar blocks.RODataColumn) error {
    35→	// The sidecar index must be within the valid range.
    36→	numberOfColumns := params.BeaconConfig().NumberOfColumns
    37→	if sidecar.Index >= numberOfColumns {
    38→		return ErrIndexTooLarge
    39→	}
    40→
    41→	// A sidecar for zero blobs is invalid.
    42→	if len(sidecar.KzgCommitments) == 0 {
    43→		return ErrNoKzgCommitments
    44→	}
    45→
    46→	// The column length must be equal to the number of commitments/proofs.
    47→	if len(sidecar.Column) != len(sidecar.KzgCommitments) || len(sidecar.Column) != len(sidecar.KzgProofs) {
    48→		return ErrMismatchLength
    49→	}
    50→
    51→	return nil
    52→}
    53→
    54→// VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs verifies if the KZG proofs are correct.
    55→// Note: We are slightly deviating from the specification here:
    56→// The specification verifies the KZG proofs for each sidecar separately,
    57→// while we are verifying all the KZG proofs from multiple sidecars in a batch.
    58→// This is done to improve performance since the internal KZG library is way more
    59→// efficient when verifying in batch.
    60→// https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/fulu/p2p-interface.md#verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs
    61→func VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs(sidecars []blocks.RODataColumn) error {
    62→	// Compute the total count.
    63→	count := 0
    64→	for _, sidecar := range sidecars {
    65→		count += len(sidecar.Column)
    66→	}
    67→
    68→	commitments := make([]kzg.Bytes48, 0, count)
    69→	indices := make([]uint64, 0, count)
    70→	cells := make([]kzg.Cell, 0, count)
    71→	proofs := make([]kzg.Bytes48, 0, count)
    72→
    73→	for _, sidecar := range sidecars {
    74→		for i := range sidecar.Column {
    75→			commitments = append(commitments, kzg.Bytes48(sidecar.KzgCommitments[i]))
    76→			indices = append(indices, sidecar.Index)
    77→			cells = append(cells, kzg.Cell(sidecar.Column[i]))
    78→			proofs = append(proofs, kzg.Bytes48(sidecar.KzgProofs[i]))
    79→		}
    80→	}
    81→
    82→	// Batch verify that the cells match the corresponding commitments and proofs.
    83→	verified, err := kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch(commitments, indices, cells, proofs)
    84→	if err != nil {
    85→		return errors.Wrap(err, "verify cell KZG proof batch")
    86→	}
    87→
    88→	if !verified {
    89→		return ErrInvalidKZGProof
    90→	}
    91→
    92→	return nil
    93→}
    94→
    95→// VerifyDataColumnSidecarInclusionProof verifies if the given KZG commitments included in the given beacon block.
    96→// https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/fulu/p2p-interface.md#verify_data_column_sidecar_inclusion_proof
    97→func VerifyDataColumnSidecarInclusionProof(sidecar blocks.RODataColumn) error {
    98→	if sidecar.SignedBlockHeader == nil || sidecar.SignedBlockHeader.Header == nil {
    99→		return ErrNilBlockHeader
   100→	}
   101→
   102→	root := sidecar.SignedBlockHeader.Header.BodyRoot
   103→	if len(root) != fieldparams.RootLength {
   104→		return ErrBadRootLength
   105→	}
   106→
   107→	leaves := blocks.LeavesFromCommitments(sidecar.KzgCommitments)
   108→
   109→	sparse, err := trie.GenerateTrieFromItems(leaves, fieldparams.LogMaxBlobCommitments)
   110→	if err != nil {
   111→		return errors.Wrap(err, "generate trie from items")
   112→	}
   113→
   114→	hashTreeRoot, err := sparse.HashTreeRoot()
   115→	if err != nil {
   116→		return errors.Wrap(err, "hash tree root")
   117→	}
   118→
   119→	verified := trie.VerifyMerkleProof(root, hashTreeRoot[:], kzgPosition, sidecar.KzgCommitmentsInclusionProof)
   120→	if !verified {
   121→		return ErrInvalidInclusionProof
   122→	}
   123→
   124→	return nil
   125→}
   126→
   127→// ComputeSubnetForDataColumnSidecar computes the subnet for a data column sidecar.
   128→// https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/fulu/p2p-interface.md#compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar
   129→func ComputeSubnetForDataColumnSidecar(columnIndex uint64) uint64 {
   130→	dataColumnSidecarSubnetCount := params.BeaconConfig().DataColumnSidecarSubnetCount
   131→	return columnIndex % dataColumnSidecarSubnetCount
   132→}
   133→
   134→// DataColumnSubnets computes the subnets for the data columns.
   135→func DataColumnSubnets(dataColumns map[uint64]bool) map[uint64]bool {
   136→	subnets := make(map[uint64]bool, len(dataColumns))
   137→
   138→	for column := range dataColumns {
   139→		subnet := ComputeSubnetForDataColumnSidecar(column)
   140→		subnets[subnet] = true
   141→	}
   142→
   143→	return subnets
   144→}

   147→func CustodyGroupCountFromRecord(record *enr.Record) (uint64, error) {

   155→		return 0, ErrCannotLoadCustodyGroupCount

1→package kzg
     2→
     3→import (
     4→	"github.com/pkg/errors"
     5→
     6→	ckzg4844 "github.com/ethereum/c-kzg-4844/v2/bindings/go"
     7→	"github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/crypto/kzg4844"
     8→)
     9→
    10→// BytesPerBlob is the number of bytes in a single blob.
    11→const BytesPerBlob = ckzg4844.BytesPerBlob
    12→
    13→// Blob represents a serialized chunk of data.
    14→type Blob [BytesPerBlob]byte
    15→
    16→// BytesPerCell is the number of bytes in a single cell.
    17→const BytesPerCell = ckzg4844.BytesPerCell
    18→
    19→// Cell represents a chunk of an encoded Blob.
    20→type Cell [BytesPerCell]byte
    21→
    22→// Commitment represent a KZG commitment to a Blob.
    23→type Commitment [48]byte
    24→
    25→// Proof represents a KZG proof that attests to the validity of a Blob or parts of it.
    26→type Proof [48]byte
    27→
    28→// Bytes48 is a 48-byte array.
    29→type Bytes48 = ckzg4844.Bytes48
    30→
    31→// Bytes32 is a 32-byte array.
    32→type Bytes32 = ckzg4844.Bytes32
    33→
    34→// CellsAndProofs represents the Cells and Proofs corresponding to a single blob.
    35→type CellsAndProofs struct {
    36→	Cells  []Cell
    37→	Proofs []Proof
    38→}
    39→
    40→// BlobToKZGCommitment computes a KZG commitment from a given blob.
    41→func BlobToKZGCommitment(blob *Blob) (Commitment, error) {
    42→	var kzgBlob kzg4844.Blob
    43→	copy(kzgBlob[:], blob[:])
    44→
    45→	commitment, err := kzg4844.BlobToCommitment(&kzgBlob)
    46→	if err != nil {
    47→		return Commitment{}, err
    48→	}
    49→
    50→	return Commitment(commitment), nil
    51→}
    52→
    53→// ComputeCells computes the (extended) cells from a given blob.
    54→func ComputeCells(blob *Blob) ([]Cell, error) {
    55→	var ckzgBlob ckzg4844.Blob
    56→	copy(ckzgBlob[:], blob[:])
    57→
    58→	ckzgCells, err := ckzg4844.ComputeCells(&ckzgBlob)
    59→	if err != nil {
    60→		return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "compute cells")
    61→	}
    62→
    63→	cells := make([]Cell, len(ckzgCells))
    64→	for i := range ckzgCells {
    65→		cells[i] = Cell(ckzgCells[i])
    66→	}
    67→
    68→	return cells, nil
    69→}
    70→
    71→// ComputeBlobKZGProof computes the blob KZG proof from a given blob and its commitment.
    72→func ComputeBlobKZGProof(blob *Blob, commitment Commitment) (Proof, error) {
    73→	var kzgBlob kzg4844.Blob
    74→	copy(kzgBlob[:], blob[:])
    75→
    76→	proof, err := kzg4844.ComputeBlobProof(&kzgBlob, kzg4844.Commitment(commitment))
    77→	if err != nil {
    78→		return [48]byte{}, err
    79→	}
    80→	return Proof(proof), nil
    81→}
    82→
    83→// ComputeCellsAndKZGProofs computes the cells and cells KZG proofs from a given blob.
    84→func ComputeCellsAndKZGProofs(blob *Blob) (CellsAndProofs, error) {
    85→	var ckzgBlob ckzg4844.Blob
    86→	copy(ckzgBlob[:], blob[:])
    87→
    88→	ckzgCells, ckzgProofs, err := ckzg4844.ComputeCellsAndKZGProofs(&ckzgBlob)
    89→	if err != nil {
    90→		return CellsAndProofs{}, err
    91→	}
    92→
    93→	return makeCellsAndProofs(ckzgCells[:], ckzgProofs[:])
    94→}
    95→
    96→// VerifyCellKZGProofBatch verifies the KZG proofs for a given slice of commitments, cells indices, cells and proofs.
    97→// Note: It is way more efficient to call once this function with big slices than calling it multiple times with small slices.
    98→func VerifyCellKZGProofBatch(commitmentsBytes []Bytes48, cellIndices []uint64, cells []Cell, proofsBytes []Bytes48) (bool, error) {
    99→	// Convert `Cell` type to `ckzg4844.Cell`
   100→	ckzgCells := make([]ckzg4844.Cell, len(cells))
   101→
   102→	for i := range cells {
   103→		ckzgCells[i] = ckzg4844.Cell(cells[i])
   104→	}
   105→	return ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch(commitmentsBytes, cellIndices, ckzgCells, proofsBytes)
   106→}
   107→
   108→// RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs recovers the complete cells and KZG proofs from a given set of cell indices and partial cells.
   109→func RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs(cellIndices []uint64, partialCells []Cell) (CellsAndProofs, error) {
   110→	// Convert `Cell` type to `ckzg4844.Cell`
   111→	ckzgPartialCells := make([]ckzg4844.Cell, len(partialCells))
   112→	for i := range partialCells {
   113→		ckzgPartialCells[i] = ckzg4844.Cell(partialCells[i])
   114→	}
   115→
   116→	ckzgCells, ckzgProofs, err := ckzg4844.RecoverCellsAndKZGProofs(cellIndices, ckzgPartialCells)
   117→	if err != nil {
   118→		return CellsAndProofs{}, errors.Wrap(err, "recover cells and KZG proofs")
   119→	}
   120→
   121→	return makeCellsAndProofs(ckzgCells[:], ckzgProofs[:])
   122→}
